source_snapshot.test_name_items: SOL session by ipmitool (Check Volatile Bit Rate rate)
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus  -U <User> -P <Password> -H <IP address> sol info
Check Volatile Bit Rate should be 115200.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Check Volatile Bit Rate Procedures & Criteria should match below:
    Volatile Bit Rate (kbps)        : 115.2
2. Output should have human readable characters.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- SOL session by ipmitool (Check Volatile Bit Rate rate): open a SOL session via ipmitool and verify the negotiated volatile bit rate (ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sol info 2>&1) then ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sol activate 2>&1 | head -n 40; SOL is interactive.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return `ipmitool sol info` (bit-rate parameters) + the first SOL console lines so the user confirms the SOL session + volatile bit rate are correct.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL identifies ipmitool, the rate query and live stream, but hard-codes cipher 17, exposes the password, assumes option support and uses `head` as interactive-session control without endpoint, owner or cleanup verification.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / IMPROVED correctly adds target/channel/ttyS0 identity, protected authentication, operator approval, bounded session handling, recovery and preserved logs. This review retains that classification and makes the two source criteria independent checkpoints.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 835/2291 repeats the partial label and truncated command, leaving syntax, target and runtime validation for later; it does not resolve session ownership, exact rate evidence or deterministic termination.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-998 draft was inspected only as history. It changed the case to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because parsing and PTY capture can be scripted, but under the repository contract the missing ipmitool package/version, BMC/channel confirmation and management-console approval require package/user confirmation.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 treats tool/channel data as readiness rather than permanent blockage; ED-35 preserves the specified ipmitool method and any Project Override coverage difference; ED-38 requires protected credentials, explicit confirmation, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Using the Project-supported ipmitool client against the intended BMC SOL channel, independently prove that the configured volatile bit rate is 115.2 kbps (115200 bps) and that a bounded live SOL session yields correct human-readable console characters.
original_method: Validate target, channel and installed ipmitool syntax; capture the complete read-only `sol info` result; compare the volatile field to 115.2 kbps without confusing it with the non-volatile field; then, after ownership approval, activate one bounded session, capture expected target-specific console output and terminate it cleanly.
manual_activity: An engineer supplies and approves the BMC/channel/console identity, installed ipmitool options, expected rate/output, session ownership and recovery. After approval, an agent can collect the read-only parameter output and run one bounded PTY session, but the engineer owns the final verdict.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC and host identity, firmware, management address/MAC/certificate and mapping among LAN interface, SOL channel/payload and host serial console
Installed ipmitool package/version/build provenance and supported `lanplus`, authentication/cipher and SOL subcommand options
Project-approved expected volatile rate of 115.2 kbps/115200 bps, precise output-label interpretation and distinction from non-volatile rate
Protected credential injection, privilege requirement and trusted management network
Current SOL enabled/active state, session owner, takeover prohibition/approval, timeout, documented escape, stale-session recovery and independent KVM/OOB access
Expected target-specific banner/prompt or known console text, encoding/line discipline, transcript redaction and a pinned reviewed Script revision if the internal Script is selected
safety_requirements: Do not copy the source or DeepSeek credential form with a literal password in command history, process listings or evidence; use the installed version's approved protected method and redact authentication output.
Bind BMC and SOL-channel identity before accepting rate output or activating the console; another BMC/channel cannot satisfy this case.
Do not hard-code cipher suite 17 unless that exact target and client combination is approved and supported.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL. Preserve a baseline and correlate deltas because deletion destroys evidence.
Treat `sol info` as a read-only configuration checkpoint only. It does not prove live readable output, and live output does not by itself prove the volatile-rate field.
Do not confuse `Volatile Bit Rate` with `Non-Volatile Bit Rate`; preserve the raw labels and values and normalize only the equivalent units 115.2 kbps and 115200 bps.
Do not activate or deactivate an owned session without explicit approval. Use an independent recovery path and send no arbitrary console input, password, break, reboot or power command.
Run activation in a PTY with a hard time bound and documented clean escape. Do not pipe the interactive client through `head`, which may close the reader without proving client/payload cleanup.

Do not automatically retry. Stop and preserve first-failure evidence on wrong identity, unsupported syntax, rate mismatch, owner conflict, unreadable/secret-bearing output, timeout or failed termination.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, identify ipmitool and BMC versions, verify supported options, bind endpoint/channel/console identity, inspect SOL state/owner and collect the complete read-only `sol info` output without changing settings.
Evaluate checkpoint A by matching the raw `Volatile Bit Rate (kbps)` field to 115.2; retain other rate fields as context but do not substitute them.
After approval, evaluate checkpoint B through exactly one bounded PTY activation, capture timestamped target-specific readable bytes and terminate with the documented escape.
Verify client exit, final payload/session state, BMC/host/recovery-path health and preserved log delta; do not issue a DUT verdict, change SOL settings, preempt a session or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Approve the ipmitool version/options, BMC/channel/console identity, expected rate and live-output signature, session ownership, timeout and recovery.
Decide whether automated character checks sufficiently establish human readability or whether an operator must confirm the transcript.
Review both independent checkpoint results and clean termination, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sol info` and `sol activate` address the two source checkpoints, but the proposed execution is not safe as written: it assumes cipher 17, exposes the password and uses `head` rather than a deterministic PTY lifecycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the installed ipmitool release's approved secret-safe authentication and documented SOL syntax. First capture full `sol info`; only after endpoint/owner approval run one bounded PTY activation with explicit escape and cleanup verification. Record the exact resolved commands for pre-execution approval.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ipmitool-specific method, source 115200 wording, Criteria 115.2 kbps wording, human-readable characters, internal Script URL and 10/0-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Identity and client preflight; full read-only `sol info`; exact volatile-field/unit evaluation; ownership approval; one bounded live SOL observation; documented escape; final state and health verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC SOL implementation, LAN interface/channel/payload, mapped host serial console and supported ipmitool release.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware and ipmitool package/version/build plus the reviewed Script revision if used.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Installed ipmitool SOL documentation and Project/vendor BMC SOL/channel specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates the source's rate and readability criteria, adds target identity, protected secrets, ownership, deterministic PTY termination and recovery without altering Master text.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A correct `sol info` rate cannot replace live readability; a readable session cannot replace the volatile-rate check; another client cannot prove ipmitool compatibility; configuration output from the wrong channel is invalid.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Client/version, endpoint/channel mapping, rate expectation, output signature, session owner, timeout/escape, security, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SOL activation can expose console data, conflict with debug/recovery ownership or leave a stale payload if lifecycle control is wrong.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve version-correct ipmitool flags, a secure credential wrapper or a pinned replacement Script, but must record original versus actual commands, reason, engineer approval and equivalent coverage. A different SOL client may validate a Project's general SOL function but does not prove the source case's ipmitool-specific coverage.
expected_evidence: BMC/host identity, management endpoint, SOL LAN interface/channel/payload/console map and pre-session active-owner state
ipmitool package/version/provenance, supported authentication options and redacted exact command metadata
Complete raw `sol info` output with the exact `Volatile Bit Rate (kbps)` label/value, unit normalization to 115200 bps and separate preservation of any non-volatile field
One timestamped bounded raw/redacted SOL transcript containing approved target-specific human-readable banner/prompt/output and encoding notes
Documented escape/close result, client exit status, final payload/session state, BMC/host/KVM/OOB health, preserved log delta and engineer-owned verdict
Pinned Script commit/hash and review result if the inaccessible internal Script is used

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure's 115200 is a baud/bps expression and Criteria's 115.2 kbps is the same expected volatile rate. Items, command and Criteria coherently require both the rate readback and a readable SOL stream; they are separate checkpoints, not contradictory purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The tool-specific objective, target class and two acceptance checkpoints are clear. Package, credentials, endpoint/channel mapping, ownership and expected output are supplyable Project execution-readiness inputs, so their absence does not make the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its useful `sol info` plus live activation concept but rejects hard-coded cipher, exposed secrets and `head`-based lifecycle control.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and its endpoint, ttyS0, protected-secret, operator and recovery safeguards; makes rate and readability evidence explicitly non-substitutable.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces deferred syntax/runtime sanity with exact field, unit, endpoint, owner and termination requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because package/client, target/channel and management-console approval are material under the repository classification contract, while retaining post-approval automation.

review_improvement: Prevents a correct rate from being used to claim readable SOL, a readable stream from masking a wrong volatile setting, or a truncated/wrong-target session from appearing successful.
independent_technical_reasoning: The parameter query is deterministic and read-only, while a PTY can mechanically inspect printable bytes. Nevertheless, this source couples a specific external client/package with protected credentials and an interactive management console that may already have an owner. Those material prerequisites and approvals make the correct repository classification package/user confirmation. The two observations must remain independent because they validate configuration and transport behavior respectively.
